name: Embedding Strategy Protocol & Registry
description: Define EmbeddingStrategy protocol in services/embedding.py with async embed(signal) -> numpy vector method. All strategies must produce vectors of the same fixed dimensionality (e.g., 128 or 256) using projection/padding as needed. Create a strategy registry that manages available strategies and runs them to populate Signal.embeddings dict (keyed by strategy name). Ensure the existing single-strategy behavior is preserved as the 'semantic' strategy.

functions.name: EmbeddingStrategyRegistry.__init__
functions.description: Construct a new EmbeddingStrategyRegistry with a fixed target dimensionality. The registry starts empty with no strategies registered. The 'semantic' strategy should be pre-registered by the application layer after construction.

inputs.name: dimensions
inputs.description: Fixed dimensionality for all embedding vectors. All registered strategies must produce vectors of this size, or their output will be projected/padded via project_to_dim.

Registry contains no registered strategies
Registry.dimensions == dimensions

functions.name: EmbeddingStrategyRegistry.register
functions.description: Register a named embedding strategy with the registry. Validates the strategy name format, checks that the object satisfies the EmbeddingStrategy @runtime_checkable Protocol, and verifies that the embed method is a coroutine function via inspect.iscoroutinefunction. Raises on invalid name, protocol non-conformance, or duplicate name.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Unique name for the strategy. Must match pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$.

validators.error_message: Strategy name must be 1-64 chars, start with lowercase letter, contain only lowercase alphanumeric and underscores.

inputs.name: strategy
inputs.description: An object conforming to the EmbeddingStrategy protocol. Must have an async embed(self, signal: Signal) -> np.ndarray method.

error_cases.name: invalid_name_format
error_cases.condition: name does not match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$

error_data.message: Strategy name must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and underscores (1-64 chars).

error_cases.name: protocol_not_satisfied
error_cases.condition: not isinstance(strategy, EmbeddingStrategy) — the object does not have an embed method with the correct signature

error_data.message: Strategy does not satisfy the EmbeddingStrategy protocol. Must have an 'embed(self, signal: Signal) -> np.ndarray' method.

error_cases.name: embed_not_async
error_cases.condition: strategy has an embed method but inspect.iscoroutinefunction(strategy.embed) is False

error_data.message: Strategy.embed must be an async coroutine function (defined with 'async def').

error_cases.name: duplicate_name
error_cases.condition: A strategy with the same name is already registered

error_data.message: A strategy with name '{name}' is already registered. Use unregister() first to replace it.

preconditions: name matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$
strategy satisfies isinstance(strategy, EmbeddingStrategy) via @runtime_checkable
strategy.embed is a coroutine function (inspect.iscoroutinefunction(strategy.embed) is True)
name is not already registered in this registry
postconditions: Strategy is stored in the registry under the given name
list_strategies() includes the newly registered strategy
Strategy can be invoked via embed() or embed_all()

functions.name: EmbeddingStrategyRegistry.embed_all
functions.description: Run all registered strategies concurrently on the given signal using asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True). Validates each result for correct shape (dimensions,) and dtype (float32 or float64). Strategies that raise exceptions or produce invalid output are skipped with logging. Returns a result containing successful embeddings and failure details.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: The signal to embed using all registered strategies.

postconditions: Result.embeddings contains only vectors with shape (dimensions,) and dtype in {float32, float64}

functions.name: project_to_dim
functions.description: Shared utility function for truncation/padding of a vector to a target dimensionality, followed by L2 normalization. If the input vector is longer than target_dim, it is truncated to the first target_dim elements. If shorter, it is zero-padded on the right. After projection, the vector is L2-normalized (unless it is a zero vector, in which case it remains zero). This is a static/standalone function, not bound to a registry instance.

inputs.name: vector
inputs.description: Input numpy vector to project. Must be 1-D.

inputs.name: target_dim
inputs.description: Target dimensionality for the output vector.

validators.error_message: target_dim must be between 1 and 4096 inclusive.

error_cases.name: not_1d_array
error_cases.condition: vector.ndim != 1

error_data.message: Expected 1-D array, got {ndim}-D array with shape {shape}.

error_cases.name: invalid_dtype
error_cases.condition: vector.dtype not in {float32, float64}

error_data.message: Expected float32 or float64 dtype, got {dtype}.

error_cases.name: invalid_target_dim
error_cases.condition: target_dim < 1 or target_dim > 4096 or not isinstance(target_dim, int)

error_data.message: target_dim must be an integer between 1 and 4096 inclusive.

error_cases.name: empty_vector
error_cases.condition: vector has length 0 (vector.shape == (0,))

error_data.message: Input vector must have at least one element.

preconditions: vector is a 1-D numpy array (vector.ndim == 1)
vector has dtype float32 or float64
target_dim is a positive integer within [1, 4096]
postconditions: Returned vector has shape (target_dim,)
Returned vector has the same dtype as the input vector
If input vector is longer than target_dim, output is first target_dim elements (truncated), then L2-normalized
If input vector is shorter than target_dim, output is zero-padded on the right, then L2-normalized
If input vector has length == target_dim, output is L2-normalized input
If input vector is all zeros, output is all zeros with shape (target_dim,)
L2 norm of output is approximately 1.0 (within 1e-6) or exactly 0.0 for zero vectors

functions.name: EmbeddingStrategyRegistry.populate_signal_embeddings
functions.description: Convenience method that runs embed_all on a signal and returns a new Signal instance with the embeddings dict populated. Since Signal is a frozen Pydantic model, this creates a copy with updated embeddings. Embeddings are converted from ndarray to list[float] for serialization safety.

inputs.description: The signal to embed and populate.

postconditions: Returned Signal is a new instance (frozen model copy) with embeddings populated

invariants: All embedding vectors produced by any registered strategy and stored in Signal.embeddings have exactly registry.dimensions elements
All embedding vectors have dtype float32 or float64 when in ndarray form
The 'semantic' strategy, when registered, preserves backward-compatible behavior of the original single-strategy embedding system
Strategy names are unique within a registry instance and match the pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$
Signal.embeddings stores vectors as list[float] (not numpy arrays) for Pydantic v2 frozen model serialization safety
project_to_dim always produces L2-normalized vectors (norm ≈ 1.0) unless the input is a zero vector
embed_all never raises due to individual strategy failures — failures are logged and reported in the result
EmbeddingStrategyRegistry is a plain class, not a singleton — multiple independent registries can coexist
All registered strategies must pass the @runtime_checkable isinstance check and inspect.iscoroutinefunction check at registration time
